patch_description:
The original algorithm sends every partition of data independently along the shortest path to each destination, paying full price for shared links multiple times (once per destination, once per partition). The key improvement is to recognize that transfers over links already used by the broadcast can piggyback at no additional link setup — i.e., build a shared broadcast (Steiner-like) tree instead of independent shortest paths.

I implement the classic Takahashi–Matsuyama Steiner tree heuristic: start with the source, repeatedly connect the nearest unconnected destination to the current tree using Dijkstra, but treat edges already in the tree as cost ~0 (they only need to be "paid" once, then all traffic riding them reuses the established transfer). This drastically reduces redundant transfers across destinations that share network paths (e.g., inter-cloud backbone links), which is exactly the "reduce redundant transfers / balance load across networks" objective. Every partition then rides the same shared tree, so the total edge cost is paid essentially once per shared link rather than multiplied per destination/partition. The output format (per-dst, per-partition edge lists) is preserved exactly, so downstream evaluation still works.
